definition.name: DNA fragmentation and sequencing-adapter introduction
definition.substrate: DNA-bearing material entering sequencing-library preparation, including enriched bead-bound chromatin or purified amplified cDNA; retain each use’s material association and separate reaction branches.
definition.operation: Convert the supplied DNA-bearing material into fragments bearing introduced sequencing-adapter sequence for subsequent library processing. Account for preparatory substrate handling included in the selected unit, such as washing bead-bound chromatin before the fragmentation/tagging reaction.
definition.mechanism_unknown_reason: This is a shared-purpose definition at the input-to-adapter-bearing-fragment stage. No common mechanism for the entire selected units is asserted. Individual uses retain their supported mechanisms: ChIPmentation includes solute-removal washes followed by Tn5 tagmentation; Drop-seq delegates Nextera XT transposome tagmentation. Null does not mean either individual reaction mechanism is scientifically unknown, nor does this relation assert that the mechanisms are equal or different.
definition.output: Reaction products containing DNA fragments with introduced sequencing-adapter sequence, with bead association, mixture composition, provenance and branch multiplicity retained as applicable; an intermediate for later library recovery and/or amplification.
definition.information_effect: Changes DNA fragment boundaries and adds adapter sequence that supplies an interface to subsequent sequencing-library processing. Retention or disruption of pre-existing biological attribution and molecular-identifier linkage is assessed on each use and relevant fragment subset; universal quantitative information retention is not assumed.
definition.purpose: Produce sequencing-adapter-bearing DNA fragments from the selected DNA-containing input for subsequent sequencing-library construction.
definition.context_requirements: Membership requires evidence for both DNA fragmentation and sequencing-adapter introduction within the selected input-to-output unit, and their sequencing-library function. Include any preparatory actions actually inside that unit. Preserve substrate form, conditioning, branch structure, identity carriers, output association and downstream dependencies on each use. Exact support, enzyme brand, dose, buffer, timing and assay position are implementation properties rather than membership requirements.

members.rationale: The entire supplied tagment_v1 unit prepares LiCl-washed version 1 immunoprecipitated beads by two cold Tris washes, then fragments/tags their chromatin DNA with Nextera enzyme. It produces the same chosen IP’s adapter-bearing bead/chromatin preparation for later recovery and amplification. Its wash mechanism, on-bead reaction, histone-target alternatives and inherited IP provenance are preserved. Direct fragment/tagging purpose is supported without a claim that this complete wash-plus-reaction mechanism equals the Drop-seq reaction. Relevant parent-context uncertainty is the transposase payload/end structure; enzyme identification and subsequent nick translation are cited, and this gap limits product-chemistry/substitution claims rather than blocking the purpose membership.

evidence.quote: The chosen ChIP protocol was followed until the beads carrying immunoprecipitated chromatin were washed with LiCl-containing wash buffer (WBIII for ChIP version 1, RIPA-LiCl for ChIP version 2, and TF-WBIII for ChIP version 3, as described in the Supplementary Note).
evidence.rationale: Locates the supplied version 1 input after WBIII and before Tris washing. References to other ChIP versions describe other routes; this assignment retains version 1 only.

evidence.quote: Beads were then washed twice with 10 mM cold Tris-Cl pH 8.0 to remove detergent, salts, and EDTA.
evidence.rationale: These two preparatory washes are consequential actions inside the supplied tagment_v1 selection. Their solute-removal purpose is reported; exchange of surrounding solution while retaining bead-associated chromatin is inferred. They remain part of this membership even though the shared category is defined by the library-preparation outcome.

evidence.quote: Subsequently, beads were resuspended in 30 μl of the tagmentation reaction buffer (10 mM Tris, pH 8.0, 5 mM MgCl_(2)) containing 1 μl Tagment DNA Enzyme from the Nextera DNA Sample Prep Kit (Illumina) and incubated at 37°C for 10 minutes in a thermocycler.
evidence.rationale: Reports the on-bead reaction, Nextera reagent, buffer composition, volume, time and temperature. These are implementation properties, not required conditions for the purpose category.

evidence.quote: The development of a hyperactive Tn5 transposase that enables simultaneous DNA fragmentation and adapter tagging (“tagmentation”) presents an opportunity for faster and more sensitive library preparation from purified DNA^(3).
evidence.rationale: Names the coupled fragmentation/tagging mechanism discussed by the authors. Its use on immunoprecipitated bead-bound chromatin is established by p00016 and supplement p00005; this does not make the preparatory washes an enzyme reaction.

evidence.quote: In ChIPmentation (right), the sequencing adapters are introduced in a single step by tagmentation of bead-bound chromatin.
evidence.rationale: Directly supports adapter introduction on bead-bound chromatin and its library-preparation function, the positive membership criterion.

evidence.quote: ChIP version 1 (used for H3K4me3 and H3K27me3) Cells were washed once with PBS and fixed with 1% paraformaldehyde in up to 1 ml PBS for 5 minutes at room temperature.
evidence.rationale: Reports the version 1 histone-target scope and upstream fixation. The target is chosen per IP, not combined into a new target; retained crosslinking at the selected boundary is inferred using the later reverse-crosslinking order in main p00016.

evidence.quote: The lysate was adjusted to 200 μl per IP with a buffer composition of 20 mM HEPES, 0.1% SDS, 1%Triton X-100, 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA, 0.5 mM EGTA and incubated with an antibody against H3K4me3 (1 μg/IP, Diagenode pAb-003-050) or H3K27me3 (1 μg/IP, Diagenode pAb-195-050) overnight at 4°C on a rotator.
evidence.rationale: Preserves separate H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 antibody choices and per-IP lineage. This upstream molecular selection is inherited provenance, not cell barcoding created by tagmentation.

evidence.quote: 20 μl of Protein A (or Protein G, dependent on the antibody used) magnetic beads were blocked overnight with 0.1% BSA in PBS and added to the IP the next day for 2 hours on a rotator at 4°C to capture the immunoprecipitated fragments.
evidence.rationale: Defines the bead-supported precursor and antibody-dependent Protein A/G alternative; the tagmented population descends from that selected IP.

evidence.quote: sonicated in a 130 μl microTUBE (for up to 3 x 106 cells) on a Covaris S220 for 12 minutes until most of the fragments were 200-700 base pairs long
evidence.rationale: Reports precursor sonication and size context only. The 200–700-bp range does not establish the immediate post-tagmentation distribution.

evidence.quote: The immunoprecipitated chromatin was washed subsequently with WBI (20 mM HEPES, 150 mM NaCl, 0.1% SDS, 0.1% DOC, 1% Triton X-100, 1 mM EDTA, 0.5 mM EGTA) (twice), WBII (20 mM HEPES, 500 mM NaCl, 0.1% SDS, 0.1% DOC, 1% Triton X-100, 1 mM EDTA, 0.5 mM EGTA) (once), WBIII (20 mM HEPES, 250 mM LiCl, 0.5% DOC, 0.5% NP-40, 1 mM EDTA, 0.5 mM EGTA) (once), and WBIV (20 mM HEPES, 1 mM EDTA, 0.5 mM EGTA) (twice).
evidence.rationale: Supplies version 1 wash context. Main p00016 inserts ChIPmentation after the LiCl wash, so WBIV is deferred until after tagmentation, rather than silently included in the input history.

evidence.quote: Following tagmentation, the beads were washed twice with 150 μl cold WBI (ChIP version 1), RIPA (ChIP version 2), or TF-WBI (ChIP version 3). Afterward, the chosen ChIP protocol was resumed with the final bead wash, elution from beads, reverse-crosslinking, and DNA purification.
evidence.rationale: Places recovery outside the selected incubation output. The immediate product is still the treated bead/chromatin preparation in its reaction mixture; retained crosslinks and continuity of the selected IP are inferred from this order.

evidence.quote: 4. Remove tagmentation reaction and wash beads twice with WBI (ChIP version 1),
evidence.rationale: Confirms reaction removal and WBI washing as subsequent handling, not an unrecorded purified-DNA output of tagment_v1.

evidence.quote: We reasoned that performing tagmentation directly on the immunoprecipitated and bead-bound chromatin would allow chromatin proteins to protect the DNA from excessive tagmentation.
evidence.rationale: Retains the authors’ tentative protection rationale without converting it into universal measured protection or a mechanism shared with soluble cDNA.

evidence.quote: Kapa HiFi HotStart ReadyMix was incubated at 98°C for 45 s prior to preparation of the PCR reaction to activate the hot-start enzyme for successful nick translation in the first PCR step.
evidence.rationale: The subsequent amplification includes nick translation. Together with the separate enzyme identification in p00016, this limits interpretation of the immediate product: exact loaded adapter strands, covalent end architecture and repaired-end sequence remain unresolved here and are not inferred from later primer or nick-translation descriptions.

assignment.scope_note: Purpose-level retrieval of transformations that produce sequencing-adapter-bearing DNA fragments, across distinct materials and local operation boundaries. The ChIPmentation member includes both cold Tris washes and the on-bead reaction; the Drop-seq member retains all four independent cDNA reactions through their immediate outputs. Shared purpose covers these entire supplied transformations without deleting the preparatory handling or asserting a common complete mechanism. Observed coupled transposome fragmentation/tagging is retained on uses; simultaneity and enzyme identity are not defining requirements at this level. A wash alone, neutralization alone or downstream amplification alone does not establish the required conversion. Product end chemistry, quantitative recovery and barcode linkage require individual evidence. This category establishes neither experimental substitution, compatibility, ancestry, literature novelty nor an executable reaction recipe.
lookup_queries: DNA cDNA chromatin transposase tagmentation fragmentation adapter addition
assignment.distinction: No existing definition is available. Admit one functional conversion category because it supports comparing preparation of adapter-bearing DNA fragments across assays; retain on-bead conditioning, chromatin/crosslink status, target attribution and recovery dependencies as properties. A separate label for version 1, antibody choice, bead reagent or 37°C recipe is unnecessary for this question. A shared-mechanism assignment across the supplied units would require accounting for the two washes as well as the reaction; a common tagmentation verb/enzyme family alone would not do so. The chosen shared-purpose claim accounts for all actions and asserts no equality or difference of complete mechanisms.

properties_to_preserve: Selected unit tagment_v1 spans beads_v1 after version 1 LiCl/WBIII washing through two cold Tris washes and enzyme incubation to tagged_beads_v1; no internal purified-DNA state is invented.

Input lineage: version 1 clarified sonicated chromatin, most precursor fragments 200–700 bp, 200 μl per IP. Upstream 1% paraformaldehyde fixation; crosslinks inferred to remain until later reversal. Precursor size is not immediate product size.

Retain H3K4me3 (1 μg/IP, Diagenode pAb-003-050) OR H3K27me3 (1 μg/IP, pAb-195-050) as separate selected-antibody alternatives, overnight 4°C IP; inherited selected-IP/sample/replicate provenance is contextual attribution rather than newly introduced cell identity.
Capture context: 20 μl Protein A or antibody-dependent Protein G magnetic beads, blocked overnight in 0.1% BSA/PBS and captured 2 h at 4°C. Chromatin is bead-associated at both selected interfaces.

Pre-input wash history WBI twice, WBII once, WBIII once (250 mM LiCl), with detergent/chelator context given in supplement p00039. Conventional final WBIV wash is deferred by the insertion boundary. Preparatory two cold 10 mM Tris-Cl pH 8.0 washes remove detergent, salts and EDTA; solution exchange is inferred without adding an unreported separation method.

Observed mechanism: Tn5-coupled DNA fragmentation and adapter tagging after the preparatory washes. Reaction 30 μl, 10 mM Tris pH 8.0, 5 mM MgCl2, 1 μl Nextera Tagment DNA Enzyme, 37°C 10 min in thermocycler. These values do not define the purpose category.

Immediate output retains the selected enriched bead/chromatin preparation in its reaction mixture, before reaction removal, two 150-μl WBI washes, final ChIP wash, elution, reverse-crosslinking and purification. It is not an eluted, repaired, amplified or size-selected final library.

Information effect: adapter sequence addition and changed DNA boundaries within the IP-selected population; direct material lineage supports IP attribution. No new cell barcode/UMI, universal preservation of all original fragments or quantitative recovery is asserted.

Authors’ chromatin-protein protection rationale is tentative as worded. Exact loaded transposase adapter strands, covalent end architecture/index content and complete nick-repair intermediate remain unresolved here; downstream primer designs and first-PCR nick translation do not establish the immediate enzyme payload.

The manufacturer mechanism is contextual support for the delegated conversion. All four direct products remain separate reaction mixtures before neutralization and custom 3′-end PCR; they are not four cell identities or a pooled final library.

evidence.quote: To prepare 3’-end cDNA fragments for sequencing, four aliquots of 600 pg of cDNA were used as input in four standard Nextera XT tagmentation reactions (Illumina, cat #FC-131-1096), performed
evidence.rationale: Reports the purpose, four distinct 600-pg inputs and four reactions. All four branches are members of this one supplied occurrence; they are not pooled at the selected output, assigned to individual cells, or replaced by the guide’s generic 1-ng input.

evidence.quote: according to the manufacturer’s instructions except that 200 nM of the custom primers P5_TSO_Hybrid and Nextera_N701 (Table S6) were used in place of the kit’s provided oligonucleotides.

evidence.quote: During this step, input DNA is tagmented (tagged and fragmented) by the Nextera XT transposome. The Nextera XT transposome simultaneously fragments the input DNA and adds adapter sequences to the ends, allowing amplification by PCR in subsequent steps.

Applying that mechanism and intermediate-product interpretation to the paper’s delegated Nextera XT cDNA reactions is inferred from supplement p00007–p00008; it supports the shared purpose without establishing the historical revision or equality of whole selected mechanisms.

evidence.quote: 9 Place the NTA plate in a thermal cycler and run the following program: NOTE Make sure that the thermal cycler lid is heated during the incubation. • 55°C for 5 minutes • Hold at 10°C. 10 When the sample reaches 10°C, proceed immediately to Neutralize NTA as the transposome is still active.
evidence.rationale: Reports the registered guide’s heated-lid thermal program and still-active reaction before immediate neutralization. These are manufacturer context, not independently verified historical Drop-seq conditions; neutralization is downstream of the selected tagmentation boundary.

evidence.quote: The cDNA was fragmented and amplified for sequencing with the Nextera XT DNA sample prep kit (Illumina) using custom primers that enabled the specific amplification of only the 3’ ends (Table S6).
evidence.rationale: Reports original fragmentation and the downstream custom 3′-end amplification function. The complete tagmentation mixture includes fragments outside the subsequently selected 3′ subset; the selected transformation itself does not perform that PCR selection.

evidence.quote: The samples were then amplified as follows: 95 oC for 30 sec; 11 cycles of 95 oC for 10 sec, 55 oC for 30 sec, 72 oC for 30 sec; then a final extension step of 72 oC for 5 min. Pairs of the 4 aliquots were pooled together, and then purified using 0.6x Agencourt AMPure XP Beads according to the manufacturer’s instructions, and eluted in 10 μL of water.
evidence.rationale: Places custom library PCR, pairwise pooling and cleanup downstream. The four direct tagmentation products remain separate reaction mixtures at the supplied output.

decisions.explanation: New shared-purpose assignment for the complete selected unit, including both Tris washes and the enzyme reaction. Both supplied selections are positive boundary examples; this cohort provides no source-demonstrated negative example, so none is invented. The comparison annotations were treated as unreviewed interpretations: reported bead/target context, inferred retained crosslinks/provenance and unknown end architecture were checked against reopened original passages. The relevant payload gap limits chemistry and substitution claims. Other inherited gaps concerning IgG control matching, production-PCR waveform, replicate thresholds or peak-calling representations are outside this selected transformation and supply no membership premise.

properties_to_preserve: Selected unit tagmentation consumes nextera_inputs and produces tagged_cdna; retains FOUR distinct 600-pg physical aliquots from the same quantified, purified amplified-cDNA parent pool and FOUR direct reaction products. Unused parent material is not duplicated into aliquots.

Parent is STAMP-derived cDNA amplified in bulk, cleaned with 0.6x AMPure XP, water eluted and pooled according to intended STAMP number before quantification. Soluble bulk and double-stranded PCR-product form at the selected input are inferred from this lineage; an aliquot is not one cell or one bead.

Observed mechanism is Nextera XT transposome-coupled fragmentation and adapter-end addition, inferred for the original reaction from explicit standard-kit delegation and the registered guide. Original kit FC-131-1096; no unsupported additional enzyme identity, cut-site rule or independent ligation intermediate is added.

Upstream 12-base cell barcode, 8-base UMI and bead/template-switch priming-handle information are inherited in amplified cDNA. Relevant end-containing fragments can retain barcode/UMI-to-transcript linkage; fragmentation can separate other transcript sequence from that end. Every immediate fragment is not claimed to carry complete identifiers.

Immediate output is four separate adapter-tagged cDNA reaction mixtures before neutralization and later custom library PCR. Products outside the later selected 3′-end subset remain part of the selected output. Pairwise pooling occurs only after subsequent PCR, with final two-aliquot combination after cleanup.

Registered Rev.D manufacturer context: TD 10 μl, ATM 5 μl, heated lid, 55°C 5 min, then 10°C hold and immediate neutralization while transposome remains active. decisions.explanation: New assignment to the same purpose definition, ID, relation, scope and aliases as the other decision; no intermediate registry commit is simulated. All four original inputs and immediate products remain represented, including fragments that later custom PCR will exclude. Manufacturer mechanism is contextual, with application to the original intermediate marked inferred; historical guide revision and reaction volumes remain unknown. The shared-purpose relation makes no common complete-mechanism claim and no substitution claim. Annotation unknowns about quantitative identifier retention and intermediate distribution remain unknown. Other inherited gaps about fabrication, bead synthesis, cell concentrations, early RT/PCR details, sequencing configuration, decoding and characterization do not determine this selection’s purpose membership.
